workflowRecommendation: Strictly sequential, one branch, one pull request: implement -> test -> review round 1 (COMMENT) -> implementer pushes the .legion/ deletion -> review round 2 (APPROVE by SHA) -> retro (one docs/solutions/ file) -> merger publishes READY. No build, no test suite, no formatter: every check is a byte-exact read of GitHub.
concerns: The working-copy commit @ carries the daemon-provisioned, empty .omp/config.yml (tracked; the repo has no .gitignore). It must never reach GitHub: commit only with path-limited `jj split -m <msg> <paths>` (the remainder, including .omp/config.yml, stays in @) and point the bookmark at the split-off commit with `-r @-`, never at @. jj also refuses to push @ because it has no description.
Anything written under $LEGION_WORKSPACE is auto-snapshotted into @. Scratch files (PR body, review body.json) go under /tmp.

GitHub main was 373184959b7a62c7e283f131564b8aeaad9365a2 when planned. LEGSMOKE-129 runs concurrently on this daemon under a different file name and may merge first; a newer main is NOT a rebase trigger. Only GitHub-reported CONFLICTING is.

The ci `check` job sleeps 20 s; check-runs are in_progress right after a push. Wait with `legion gh -- pr checks <n> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --watch` before reading conclusions. A red run is re-run with `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never by pushing.
The spec requires both thermonuclear reviews once even though the diff is a single .md file; the docs-only Thermo exemption is not taken because pipeline coverage is the deliverable.
No handoff is written after .legion/ is deleted: the cleanup push, the APPROVE, retro, and the merger report with `legion handoff complete` alone. Recreating .legion/ restarts the review loop.
